entries.a: A major scale has seven notes, and with the sharps and flats an octave has twelve.
An octave is the gap between one note and the next note with the same name, where the frequency doubles.
The natural notes are A, B, C, D, E, F and G, then it starts again.
A chord is three or more notes played together.
Tempo is the speed of a piece of music. BPM means beats per minute.
The treble clef is the symbol at the start of the staff for higher notes, like the right hand on a piano.
A symphony is a long piece for a full orchestra, usually in four parts, called movements.
An orchestra is a large group of musicians in four sections: strings, woodwind, brass and percussion.
Jazz is a style born in New Orleans in the early 1900s, built on improvisation and swing.
The blues is a style that grew out of African American communities in the Deep South, with twelve bar patterns and sad, honest lyrics.
An opera is a play told entirely through singing, with an orchestra.
A cappella means singing without any instruments.
A violin has four strings.
A standard bass guitar has four strings.
A cello has four strings.
A concert harp has forty seven strings.
The Beatles were four people from Liverpool: John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr.
Bohemian Rhapsody is by Queen, written by Freddie Mercury, released in 1975.
Freddie Mercury was the lead singer of Queen, famous for his four octave range and showmanship.
Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was an Austrian composer from the 1700s who wrote hundreds of works and started composing as a small child.
Ludwig van Beethoven was a German composer, famous for nine symphonies. He kept composing after he went deaf.
Johann Sebastian Bach was a German Baroque composer of the 1700s, famous for the Brandenburg Concertos and his organ music.
The Four Seasons was composed by Antonio Vivaldi, an Italian, in the 1720s.
The Moonlight Sonata is by Beethoven.
Michael Jackson is known as the King of Pop.
Elvis Presley is known as the King of Rock and Roll.
Michael Jackson's Thriller, from 1982, is usually named as the best selling album of all time.
The Beatles are often listed among the best selling artists ever, with Elvis Presley and Michael Jackson close behind.
Taylor Swift is an American singer-songwriter who began in country music and became one of the biggest pop stars in the world.
Adele is an English singer-songwriter known for powerful ballads like Someone Like You and Hello.
Ed Sheeran is an English singer-songwriter famous for songs like Shape of You.
ABBA were a Swedish pop group, famous for Dancing Queen. The name is the first letters of the band members' names.
Rammstein is a German industrial metal band, famous for their big fiery stage shows.
Hans Zimmer is a German film composer who scored Inception, Interstellar and The Lion King.
John Williams is the American composer behind the Star Wars music, as well as Jaws, Indiana Jones and Harry Potter.
A guitar is a stringed instrument, usually with six strings, played by plucking or strumming.
Dubstep is a style of electronic dance music with heavy bass and a slow, wobbling beat.
EDM means electronic dance music, made for clubs and festivals.
A decibel is the unit used to measure how loud a sound is.
A metronome is a device that clicks at a steady speed to help musicians keep time.
Karaoke is singing along to a backing track while the words appear on screen. The word is Japanese.
Acoustic means played without electric amplification or electronics.
